sections.title: Introduction
sections.extract: \label{sec-intro} Let us recall the history of the Hecke algebra from the perspectives of algebraization and categorification.

sections.title: The Hecke algebra by generators and relations
sections.extract: Let $G$ be a split finite reductive group over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $B \subset G$ be a Borel subgroup. A fundamental object in representation theory is the Hecke algebra \[ \mathrm{Fun}_{B \times B}(G, \mathbb{C}) \] of $B$-biinvariant complex valued functions on $G$, with multiplication given by convolution. This algebra first emerged when studying the irreducible complex characters of $G$, but

sections.title: The Hecke category
sections.extract: Beginning with the seminal work \cite{KaL1} of Kazhdan and Lusztig it was realised that the Hecke algebra admits a categorification, which has come to be known as the Hecke category. According to Grothendieck's function-sheaf dictionary, the algebra of $B$-biinvariant functions on $G$ should be categorified by some version of $B$-biequivariant sheaves on $G$. sections.title: Soergel bimodules by generators and relations
sections.extract: A \emph{Bott-Samelson bimodule} is a bimodule of the form $B_{\un{w}} \define B_s \ot_R B_t \ot_R \cdots \ot_R B_u$ for an expression $\un{w}=st\dots u$. They form a full monoidal subcategory of $R-\Bim$, which we denote $\BSBim$. By definition, any Soergel bimodule is a direct sum of shifts of summands of bimodules in $\BSBim$. sections.title: The standard trace and the defect formula
sections.extract: \label{subsec-defectformula} A \emph{trace} on $\HB$ is a $\Zvv$-linear map $\e \co \HB \to \Zvv$ satisfying $\e(hh') = \e(h'h)$ for all $h,h' \in \HB$. A straightforward calculation shows that the map $\e(\sum c_w H_w) = c_e$ is a trace, called the \emph{standard trace}.
